passage.title: Umar ibn al-Khattab: The Just Caliph
paras: Umar ibn al-Khattab was born in Makkah into the Quraysh tribe. As a young man he was known for his strength, his courage and his sharp mind. At first he was a fierce opponent of Islam, but after hearing verses of the Qur'an he accepted Islam, and the Muslims of Makkah were strengthened by his support.

The Prophet ﷺ gave him the title al-Faruq, the one who distinguishes truth from falsehood. Umar became one of the Prophet's closest companions, and his daughter Hafsah became one of the Prophet's wives.

After the death of Abu Bakr, Umar became the second caliph in 634 CE (13 AH). He led the Muslims for about ten years. During his caliphate the Muslim state grew greatly, but he is remembered above all for how he governed.

Umar set up a register (diwan) so that people received regular support from the treasury. He began dating events from the Hijrah, creating the Islamic calendar. He appointed judges, founded new towns and organised the state's finances. He is said to have walked the streets at night to see the needs of the people for himself, and he held his governors to account.

Umar died in 644 CE after being attacked while leading the Fajr prayer. He was buried beside the Prophet ﷺ and Abu Bakr in Madinah. Muslims remember him as a just caliph who believed that power was a trust.
